A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LiveResearchBench and DeepEval. All 46 pages, including Appendices A–I, support reliable comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: v1 reports original system evaluations and citation-error measurements in Tables 1–2, human-alignment results in Appendix B, and survey findings in Appendix G.

after.justification: v4 retains these original benchmark evaluations, human-alignment results, and survey findings.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and verification pipelines, DeepEval metrics and judging procedures, and Deerflow+ modifications remain unchanged (Sections 3–4; Appendix C).

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 100-task benchmark spanning seven domains, survey coverage, and citation-accuracy evaluations on market analysis and wide information search.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2, Figure 7, and the Deerflow/Deerflow+ case study. Appendix B retains the same three candidate judges.

E3.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–B retain the same scoring rubrics, judge ensemble, position-swapped pairwise procedure, output limits, retry policy, and human-evaluation sample sizes.

E4.justification: The judge-alignment study, Deerflow case study, error-pattern examples, and presentation-checklist breakdown remain unchanged in Appendices B, C, E, and I.

E5.justification: Judge-score averaging and human-agreement reporting are unchanged. No seed information, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, Figures 6–7 and 22, and Appendix B retain identical results. For example, Open Deep Research's Table 1 average remains 73.7, and its Table 2 market-analysis total remains 91.9 citation errors.

T1.justification: Scoring definitions and mathematical thresholds remain unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs establishing additional formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark, evaluation-suite, and system-comparison contributions, including claims about weaknesses in citation reliability and analytical depth.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning judge behavior, memory and context bottlenecks, and tradeoffs among coverage, coherence, citation quality, and analytical depth are unchanged. No substantive limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-availability statement and project repository address to the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation and prompt details remain unchanged, and the Section 3.2 footnote still makes full dataset release subject to institutional approval.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to existing deep-research benchmarks, agent systems, and long-form evaluation methods.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one code-access sentence, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining prose, section sequence, and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Existing displays shift with text reflow: Figure 1 moves from page 2 to page 3, and Figure 6 from page 8 to page 9. Figures and tables retain their content and design; appendix renderings are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies a code-repository location absent from v1, modestly improving resource discoverability and reproducibility documentation. Scientific evidence and appendices are unchanged, while layout shifts have no substantial quality impact. The PDFs do not establish the repository's completeness or usability.
